title: Constantinople · circa 1200
subtitle: An independent city experience
approximation_notice: Original interpretive reconstruction. Landmark identities follow sources; coastline, relief, street plots, ordinary buildings and many monument dimensions are authored approximations. No survey accuracy, complete historical reconstruction, population or economic simulation is claimed.

landmarks.name: Hagia Sophia
landmarks.description: The Great Church, with a central dome above layered arcades. ASCE gives an approximately 31 m dome diameter and a modern geographic locator. Other model dimensions and details are approximate. Minarets and the post-1261 Deesis mosaic are absent.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Hippodrome
landmarks.description: Elongated arena with a curved southern end and monument spine. Seating, dimensions and surviving details are interpreted; this is not evidence of exact crowd counts or event schedules.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Hagia Eirene
landmarks.description: The neighboring church includes medieval rebuilding after the earthquake of 740. Domed basilican volumes are interpreted; the later Ottoman palace enclosure is absent.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Basilica Cistern
landmarks.description: A covered reservoir beneath the precinct, presented as an accessible cutaway study. It is not an exposed above-ground hall. Its exact operation and hydraulic connections in 1200 remain uncertain; model dimensions are approximate. The rendered 12 by 28 column grid is a model arrangement, awaiting checked primary dimensional documentation.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Great Palace terraces
landmarks.description: Representative courts, halls and service ranges on artificial terraces. Some older imperial functions continued after the principal court moved northwest. This assembly does not recreate a fully preserved sixth-century palace.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Boukoleon sea palace
landmarks.description: An interpreted sea-facing imperial range. The maritime relationship is historical; room plans, roof forms and quay arrangement are hypotheses.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Saints Sergius and Bacchus
landmarks.description: A sixth-century domed church in the southern city. The central mass is an original simplified interpretation, with later Ottoman additions excluded.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Column of Constantine
landmarks.description: The earlier imperial statue fell in 1105/6; Manuel I replaced it with a cross. The column retains this medieval identity without the later stone encasement. Model height is approximate.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Forum of Theodosius area
landmarks.description: A restrained public-space hypothesis west of Constantine. The column is an interpretive marker for a forum whose precise medieval extent and arrangement remain uncertain.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Myrelaion monastery church
landmarks.description: A tenth-century foundation above a substructure. Columbia reports the surviving 13.10 by 24.10 m platform. Roof, facades and surrounding plots are interpreted for the pre-1203 city.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Pantokrator monastery
landmarks.description: A Komnenian foundation with three adjoining churches, imperial burials and charitable functions. These domed ranges express that compound organization; full campus geometry is interpreted.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Church of the Holy Apostles
landmarks.description: A lost imperial church and burial complex on the western heights. The five-domed composition is an architectural hypothesis for a monument whose reconstruction remains debated.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Aqueduct of Valens
landmarks.description: An elevated arcade crossing an urban saddle. The 970 m length follows the modern bridge length cited by Ward, Crow and Crapper; spans, height, alignment and hydraulic operation are interpreted.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Blachernae imperial precinct
landmarks.description: The principal court in the northwest, represented by terraces and reception halls. Its detailed 1200 plan remains unresolved; the later Tekfur Sarayı is absent.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Blachernae sanctuary study
landmarks.description: An explicitly interpretive sanctuary beside the northwestern court and waterfront. The assembly represents a religious precinct and does not claim to reproduce the lost church exactly.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Stoudios monastery
landmarks.description: A longstanding monastic precinct in the southwest. This original spatial hypothesis restores habitation without treating the roofless present-day ruin as its condition in 1200.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Middle Byzantine church at Vefa
landmarks.description: A Middle Byzantine church with disputed original dedication. Its surviving monument identity is retained without assigning an unqualified historical name or copying all later additions.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Golden Gate approach
landmarks.description: The monumental southwestern entrance is represented by portals, flanking masses and a paved approach. The schematic original assembly omits the later Yedikule fortress.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position is snapped to the authored theodosian_inner centerline and the gate width follows its tangent; this alignment and all passage, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Central land-wall gate study
landmarks.description: An interpreted access assembly in the central defenses. The label identifies a model sector, without settling disputed gate identifications.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position is snapped to the authored theodosian_inner centerline and the gate width follows its tangent; this alignment and all passage, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Northern land-wall gate study
landmarks.description: An interpreted northern gate and city approach. Passage proportions and tower phases await sector-specific measurement.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. landmarks.name: Aetius cistern study
landmarks.description: An open reservoir represented as a sunk walled basin. Model extent and fill state are approximate; water in the model is not proof that the basin operated in 1200.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Aspar cistern study
landmarks.description: An interpreted open storage basin on the heights, treated as one part of a distributed water system rather than a complete network.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Mocius cistern study
landmarks.description: An interpreted open basin among the western wards. Its exact medieval operation and connections remain unresolved.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Neorion waterfront warehouses
landmarks.description: Storage ranges and handling yards near the Golden Horn. This original ensemble expresses maritime exchange without asserting a surveyed quay plan.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Perama landing-place study
landmarks.description: Shore access and storage hypotheses in the commercial waterfront. Concession boundaries and cargo mix remain uncertain.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.

landmarks.name: Marmara harbor study
landmarks.description: A representative working waterfront. Storage, vessels and slipway arrangements are interpretive rather than a timeless plan of the changing Marmara harbors.
landmarks.evidence: Historical identity supported. Local position, envelope, construction and surface details are interpretive unless explicitly sourced in the description. Not a survey or an exact record of condition in 1200.
